acceptance_criteria.criterion: Navigating to #/repositories/:id renders the repository overview view.
The header displays the repository name, ID, URL (as clickable external link), and a back link to #/repositories.
The table contains columns: Project, Workspace, Branch, Status, Actions.
Each Project cell is a clickable link navigating to #/projects/:pid.
Each Workspace cell is a clickable link navigating to #/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid.
Branch, Status, and Actions cells are rendered via the shared buildRepoStatusCells component.
Branch-quick-switch works on non-STABLE workspace rows; triggers a refresh on successful switch.
STABLE workspace rows show plain-text branch names.
The Refresh button re-fetches all status data and updates existing rows in-place.
An empty state message is shown when no projects contain this repository.
Individual project/workspace fetch failures are handled gracefully (partial results displayed).
The view follows the setRouter(router) / _router null-guard pattern.
The Git GUI button calls api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, repoId) correctly.
The Browse button appears when webserverUrl is configured.
No innerHTML assignments — all text set via textContent.

comments.note: repository-detail.js uses Promise.all for the initial 3 fetches then Promise.allSettled for the fan-out. This is correct for the current design. However, if the initial api.repositories.get() fails, the entire view shows a generic error paragraph rather than a more contextual 'repository not found' message — a small UX polish opportunity for a future iteration.

The doRefresh() function in repository-detail.js re-fetches status only for initialized workspaces using api.status.refresh (force-refresh). It intentionally does not re-discover new projects/workspaces that have been added since the view loaded. This is consistent with the plan's 'no polling' design decision and is the correct trade-off for a local dev tool.

The STABLE_WS_ID constant ('STABLE') is duplicated across workspace-detail.js and the new repository-detail.js. Both modules independently define the same constant. A shared constants module (e.g. utils/constants.js) would remove this duplication and reduce drift risk if the STABLE workspace ID convention ever changes.
app.js uses a mix of single-line and multi-line import styles. The new import for renderRepositoryDetail follows the established multi-line pattern. No issues introduced.

AC15 verified: the three `innerHTML = ''` usages are safe container-clearing idioms, not text injection. No textContent bypass found.

Edge-case review: (1) anyFailed toast fires only when rows.length > 0 AND anyFailed — prevents spurious warnings on empty repos. (2) container.isConnected guards present at all four async resume points — no stale DOM writes after navigation. (3) doRefresh() mutex (refreshInProgress flag) prevents double-clicks from triggering concurrent fetches. (4) CSS.escape used in updateStatusTable querySelector — safe against special characters in pid/wid values.

comments.note: The three `el.innerHTML = ''` / `container.innerHTML = ''` usages are safe container-clearing idioms (no user-supplied content injected). AC15 is correctly met — all user-visible text is set via textContent. No XSS risk.
doRefresh() is protected by a refreshInProgress mutex — rapid double-clicks cannot trigger concurrent fetches. Solid defensive coding.
CSS.escape() is applied in updateStatusTable's querySelector for pid/wid — correct handling of special characters in workspace/project IDs.

container.isConnected is checked at all 4 async resume points (after Promise.all, after loadWorkspaceRows, inside doRefresh, inside the .catch handler) — no stale DOM writes possible after the user navigates away.

summary: Full line-by-line review of repository-detail.js, app.js, and repository-detail.test.mjs. All 20 unit tests confirmed passing locally (20/20, exit 0). No blocking issues found. Code is clean, well-structured, and consistent with existing codebase patterns.
Architecture: clear three-layer structure (data loading → DOM builders → entry point). All functions are small and focused with excellent JSDoc coverage.

Best Practices: setRouter/_router null-guard applied correctly; encodeURIComponent on all URL route parameters; CSS.escape in querySelector; rel=noopener noreferrer on external links; innerHTML used only for safe container-clearing (empty assignments), never for text injection.

Performance: correct Promise.all for initial 3 parallel fetches, Promise.allSettled for fan-out per project/workspace. refreshInProgress mutex prevents concurrent refresh calls. No polling is the right trade-off for a local dev tool.

notes: All 15 acceptance criteria are met and verified by 20 passing unit tests. Key design decisions to validate during QA: (1) Branch-quick-switch context extraction via anchorEl.closest('tr').dataset.pid / .dataset.wid — requires the <tr> data attributes to be set correctly, which they are. (2) Uninitialized workspace rows render empty status cells (no badge, no action buttons) — intentional per plan spec. (3) The Refresh button updates rows in-place using updateRepoStatusCells from repo-status-cells.js component, re-using the same path as workspace-detail. (4) anyFailed warning toast only fires when there is partial data (at least one row rendered AND at least one fetch failed).
